evidence.text: Phase margin is the additional phase lag required at the gain-crossover frequency to bring a negative-feedback loop to the verge of instability. Larger positive phase margin generally indicates more relative stability and less ringing.
Gain margin is the factor by which loop gain can increase at the phase-crossover frequency before the closed loop becomes unstable. It is commonly reported in decibels.
Sampling frequency components above half the sample rate causes aliasing into the Nyquist band. An analog anti-alias filter attenuates those components before the ADC.

A local decoupling capacitor supplies transient current near an integrated circuit power pin and reduces the high-frequency impedance of the power-distribution path. Short connections minimize parasitic inductance.
A conventional SPI bus uses a serial clock, controller-out peripheral-in data, peripheral-out controller-in data, and one chip-select signal per addressed peripheral.
A first-order junction-temperature estimate is ambient temperature plus dissipated power multiplied by junction-to-ambient thermal resistance: Tj equals Ta plus P times theta-JA.
Coulomb counting estimates battery state of charge by integrating measured current over time. Sensor bias accumulates, so the estimate needs periodic correction from another observable state.
A differential pair should be routed with controlled impedance, close intra-pair spacing, and a continuous reference plane. Length matching limits timing skew between the two conductors.
Integral windup occurs when a controller integrator continues accumulating error while the actuator is saturated. Anti-windup limits or back-calculates the integrator state.
In a Kalman filter, the covariance matrix represents estimated state uncertainty. The measurement update reduces uncertainty according to measurement noise and the Kalman gain.

High-frequency return current follows the path of lowest impedance, normally close to the signal trace on its reference plane. Splits in that plane force a larger loop area and can increase emissions.

Priority inversion happens when a high-priority task waits for a resource held by a lower-priority task while medium-priority work delays the holder. Priority inheritance bounds the delay by temporarily raising the holder's priority.
